newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh storm blows down refugee camp.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh storm blows down refugee camp.

text.p: Three ships were damaged and a number of fishing boats went missing in the Bay of Bengal when a storm struck Bangladesh's main port city of Chittagong early on Sunday, port officials said.
The storm, with winds of up to 124 kph (77 mph), lashed the port around 4.30 a.m. (2230 GMT), the officials said.
A Singapore-flagged container ship, Kota Berjaya, broke loose from its mooring and struck the Banglar Kallol, a Bangladeshi ship, from the rear, port officials said.
They said Banglar Kiron, another Bangladeshi ship, slammed into a stone wall on the Karnaphuli channel.
The extent of damage to the vessels was not yet clear.
Thge 163-meter Kota Berjaya arrived in Chittagong from Singapore on March 15 and was due to leave the port on Sunday.
Police said an unspecified number of fishing boats were missing after the storm hit without warning from weather officials.

On land, the storm, accompanied by heavy rain, destroyed around 250 houses in Chittagong and Rangamati district in Chittagong Hill Tracts, and flattened a large camp for Burmese refugees in nearby Cox's Bazar.
Police said a woman and her daughter were killed when their house collapsed in Nailyachhari villages in Rangamati.
They said over 80 people were injured in Chittagong and Rangamati.
"We are awaiting details," one police officer in Chittagong told reporters.
Meanwhile, Cox's bazar officials said at least 25 inmates were injured during the storm, mostly by flying debris, at Kutupalong camp, which housed 10,000 Moslem Rohingya refugees from Burma.
"Majority of the sheds in this camp have been blown away," one refugee official told reporters in Cox's Bazar.
More than 250,000 Rohingyas fled to Bangladesh from west Burma's Moslem-majority Arakan state in early 1992 to escape alleged military persecution.
All but 23,500 have returned home since repatriation, supervised by the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, began in September that year, officials said on Sunday.
